title: Gillibrand, Schneider Call For Hearings After Navy Discloses 8 Attempted Suicides By Sailors In USS Abraham Lincoln Carrier Strike Group
text:
Today, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), a member of the Senate Armed Services and Intelligence Committees, and Representative Brad Schneider (D-IL-10), a member of the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, called for congressional hearings following the Navy’s confirmation that 8 sailors in the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group had attempted suicide during the group’s most recent deployment. This admission was made in a September 22 letter Gillibrand received from Acting United States Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao, weeks after administration officials and the president had dismissed families’ and soldiers’ concerns about conditions on board the ship. 

Acting Secretary Cao’s response follows the August 2026 letter that Gillibrand and 14 of her colleagues sent to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth calling for transparency after reporting detailed dismal conditions for sailors on board the USS Abraham Lincoln. Gillibrand also previously demanded hearings over those reports.

“What Trump and Secretary Hegseth dismissed as ‘fake news’ turned out to be serious and deteriorating conditions for our service members,” said Senator Gillibrand, member of the Senate Armed Services Committee. “Our troops and their families make immense sacrifices every single day, yet the president dismissed them with open disrespect. That this administration can find endless taxpayer dollars for bombs, ballrooms, and billionaires, but cannot take care of our service members, is completely unacceptable. The American people need hearings, accountability, and a clear plan to protect our service members and prioritize American families.”

“As the Member of Congress representing Naval Station Great Lakes in North Chicago, where every Navy recruit receives basic training, the health and well-being of our men and women in uniform is one of my highest priorities,” said Rep. Schneider. “Every American should be outraged by this Administration’s failure to equip our service members with the tools and support they need to carry out a successful deployment and the blatant lies about the conditions sailors were experiencing on the USS Abraham Lincoln. The new reporting from CNN in response to Senator Gillibrand’s oversight effort is deeply concerning and should alarm everyone. I’m glad to join Senator Gillibrand in calling for open and public hearings to get the answers the American people and our service members deserve.”

title: Gillibrand Introduces Legislation To Streamline Law Enforcement And Protect Public Safety On Seneca Nation Land
text:
Legislation Would Address A 1948 Federal Law That Granted New York State Criminal Jurisdiction Over Seneca Nation Territory, Fix Termination-Era Law Enforcement Model

Today, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand introduced the Seneca Nation Law Enforcement Efficiency Act. The bill would establish a legal mechanism to end a 1948 federal law that granted New York State criminal jurisdiction over Seneca Nation territory, helping to resolve overlapping responsibilities between federal, state, and Tribal authorities. In order to eliminate legal confusion and strengthen public safety, the Seneca Nation Law Enforcement Efficiency Act makes clear that the Seneca Nation and the U.S. attorney general must jointly agree in writing to end New York State’s criminal jurisdiction over Seneca land once the bill has been signed into law. This would give the Seneca Nation a path to more fully pursue their self-determination and self-governance on their Tribal lands.

“The Seneca Nation Law Enforcement Efficiency Act is a crucial first step in fixing a Termination-era law enforcement model that has existed for the last 78 years,” said Senator Gillibrand. “The Seneca Nation has suffered as a result, and now is Congress’ chance to right historic wrongs and end New York State’s automatic jurisdiction over Seneca lands. This bill will enhance public safety and respect Tribal sovereignty.”

“The lack of clear and effective law enforcement and criminal jurisdiction on our lands has created an environment where drug dealers, drug traffickers and other criminals have thrived at the expense of the safety of the Seneca people,” said Seneca Nation President J. Conrad Seneca. “The current archaic system of New York State jurisdiction puts our people in danger. Restoring the federal government’s treaty responsibility to work with the Seneca Nation to provide law enforcement represents a major step forward in protecting our people and our territories. We appreciate Senator Gillibrand’s willingness to listen to our concerns and work with us to introduce this important legislation in the Senate. We will not relent in our efforts to make enhanced public safety a reality on Seneca Nation lands.”

“This outdated jurisdictional framework has created real-world public safety problems,” said Congressman Nick Langworthy. “Our men and women in law enforcement are doing the best they can under challenging circumstances, but when authority is fragmented and accountability is unclear, resourceful criminals exploit the gaps and that’s exactly what we’ve seen happen. This legislation provides a targeted solution that respects tribal sovereignty, preserves federal oversight, and ensures that any change occurs only with mutual agreement. Most importantly, it will make our communities safer, and that is a goal we all share.”

More than 8,500 enrolled Seneca citizens live in New York State. For generations, the Seneca people have lived in the Finger Lakes and Genesee Valley regions of New York State and now reside in large portions of Western New York on the Allegany, Cattaraugus, and Oil Spring territories, including the cities of Buffalo and Niagara Falls.

Congressman Nick Langworthy (R-NY) leads similar legislation in the U.S. House of Representatives. 

The bill can be read HERE.

title: Ahead Of Import Ban On Some Canadian Products, Gillibrand Demands Passage Of Bill To Repeal And Refund President Trump’s Tariffs Against Canada
text:
Gillibrand’s Legislation Would Also Halt The Import Ban On Certain Canadian Dairy Products, Alcohol, and Other Goods, Which Is Set To Go Into Effect Next Week

Today, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) held a virtual press conference demanding passage of her legislation to curb President Trump’s costly trade war with Canada. This comes less than a week before a sweeping import ban on Canadian dairy products, alcohol, and motorcycles is set to take effect.

Senator Gillibrand’s legislation, the Banning Antiquated Duties and Delivering Equitable American Levies (BAD DEAL) Act, would repeal all tariffs levied under Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 and refund Americans for all duties paid under this authority. This includes President Trump’s 50% tariffs on Canada as well as his forthcoming import ban on Canadian goods.

“President Trump and Republicans promised to lower costs and make life more affordable, but they’ve used their total power in Washington to make life more expensive than ever,” said Senator Gillibrand. “Let’s be clear: the latest tariffs and impending import ban on Canadian goods are a bad deal for New York families. I’m doing everything I can to halt these tariffs and lower costs for New York families.”

President Trump’s trade war with Canada is driving up prices and harming New York families. Canada is one of New York State’s largest export markets for both goods and services, and the state imports more than $20 billion annually from Canada. Already, New York families have spent over $5,500 more due to President Trump’s tariff chaos and other reckless policies. The new 50% tariffs on Canada are projected to cost businesses and households across the U.S. up to $10 billion annually.

Senator Gillibrand introduced the BAD DEAL Act last week alongside Senator Peter Welch (D-VT). Senators Jacky Rosen (D-NV) and Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) also cosponsor the bill, and Rep. Brad Schneider (D-IL-10) introduced companion legislation in the U.S. House of Representatives in August. 

Senator Gillibrand has opposed President Trump’s tariffs since the start of his administration and worked tirelessly to get the American people their money back. Last year, she joined 14 of her colleagues in introducing the Small Business RELIEF Act to end Trump’s Tariff Tax and refund small businesses their duties paid. In March, she and her colleagues introduced the Small Business Liberation 2.0 Act to exempt small businesses from another set of Trump-imposed tariffs and refund what they had already paid.

title: Gillibrand, Schumer Blast Trump Administration For Politicizing Disaster Assistance And Denying Aid For February Blizzard
text:
Yesterday, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) and Senator Chuck Schumer (D-NY) condemned the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) for politicizing disaster assistance following its second unexplained denial of Governor Hochul’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration in the wake of the February 2026 blizzard in New York. The storm brought record snowfall, whiteout conditions, and coastal flooding to downstate New York, resulting in increased expenditure of state and local resources to help communities recover from the disastrous conditions. 

The relief provided by the declaration would have alleviated the financial burden that counties and the state took on to mitigate the impacts of the storm. Governor Hochul’s request included Public Assistance for Queens, Nassau, and Suffolk Counties, Snow Assistance for Bronx, Kings, Nassau, New York, Queens, Richmond, Suffolk, and Westchester Counties, and Hazard Mitigation for the entire state.

In a letter to the FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton, the senators called out FEMA’s July 2, 2026 denial of Hochul’s initial request, which did not provide any reasoning or justification. In fact, according to public reporting, administration officials had determined that the request met federal standards for approval, but President Trump himself denied it regardless. The senators wrote, “Reporting reveals that the regional offices at FEMA and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) determined that the February blizzard met the threshold and standards for a disaster declaration for a record-breaking snowstorm. Disturbingly, the same reporting shows that President Trump chose to overrule the findings of his own agencies, in a move that can only be described as political.”

After Governor Hochul appealed the denial, FEMA again refused her request with no explanation on September 2, 2026. The senators expressed their concern over the administration’s blatant political weaponization of federal disaster assistance, writing, “President Trump and this administration have the wrong priorities. Since taking office in his second term, President Trump has disproportionately denied or delayed approval of requests for federal disaster aid from states led by Democrats. Instead of helping all Americans to recover from record-breaking natural disasters, it is clear the President is turning his back to the millions of hard-working New Yorkers.” 

The senators concluded the letter by calling for full transparency around the Major Disaster Declaration denials. They requested that FEMA provide them with its analysis and reasoning for both the initial denial of Governor Hochul’s request and the denial of her appeal by October 5, 2026.

The full text of the letter can be found here.

title: Gillibrand Celebrates $6 Million Investment For Food Bank For NYC’s Hunts Point Food Distribution Center
text:
Today, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, member of the Senate Appropriations Committee, stood with Bronx elected officials and Food Bank For NYC to celebrate the $6 million she secured for major renovations and modernization of Food Bank For NYC’s Hunts Point Food Distribution Center in the Bronx. 

“Food Bank For NYC distributes millions of pounds of food to families, seniors, and other New Yorkers in need each year,” said Senator Gillibrand. “I’m proud to have led the effort to secure $6 million in federal funding to support the comprehensive renovation and expansion of the Hunts Point Food Distribution Center, and I’m committed to fighting for more federal resources to expand access to healthy and nutritious food, promote local job creation, and help New Yorkers thrive.” 

“This incredible investment in Food Bank For New York City’s Hunts Point warehouse is a commitment to addressing food insecurity and expanding access to nutritious food in communities that need it most,” said New York State Senator Jose M. Serrano. “This critical funding will strengthen our local food distribution infrastructure, helping ensure that Bronx families have reliable access to healthy food while improving the health and well-being of our communities. As the Senator of the 29th Senate District, I am grateful to Senator Kirsten Gillibrand and our fellow elected officials for securing this important investment for our communities.” 

“Hunts Point is not only the heart of New York City’s food system; it is critical infrastructure that millions of New Yorkers depend on every day,” said New York State Assemblymember Amanda Septimo. “This $6 million investment will strengthen that infrastructure, expand Food Bank For New York City’s ability to get millions more pounds of food to families, and ensure The Bronx continues to lead the fight against hunger across our city. At a moment when families are feeling enormous pressure at the grocery store, investments that increase our capacity to feed New Yorkers could not be more important.”

“I grew up here in the South Bronx, raised by a single mother who relied on food distributions powered by Food Bank For New York City to help us get by,” said Council Member Justin E. Sanchez. “At a time when the White House is determined to cut programs that feed New Yorkers their work is more important than ever. Senator Gillibrand’s outstanding investment will strengthen the Food Bank’s infrastructure, expand its capacity, and help ensure it can meet this moment as more New Yorkers are forced to turn to its network for support.”

“We are grateful to Senator Gillibrand for her support of vital federal food and nutrition programs and for helping secure this $6 million investment in Food Bank For New York City’s Hunts Point Food Distribution Center,” said Bob Silvia, Chief Procurement and Operations Officer at Food Bank For NYC. “Investments in both nutrition assistance programs and food distribution infrastructure are essential to ensuring that families can access food when they need it most.”

“This $6 million investment will modernize critical infrastructure at Food Bank for NYC’s Hunts Point Food Distribution Center, strengthening our city’s ability to deliver fresh, nutritious food to our families who need it most,” said Bronx Borough President Vanessa L. Gibson. “Even as this White House administration cuts critical funding to social safety net programs, I am proud to see our federal legislators standing up for everyday New Yorkers and supporting projects that will help us combat hunger in our communities. Thank you to Senator Gillibrand for her advocacy and continued commitment to bringing federal resources to the Bronx.”

Food Bank For NYC is the city’s largest hunger relief organization, and its 90,000 square foot Hunts Point Distribution Center is the city’s largest hunger relief logistics hub. Last year, more than 90 million pounds of food was distributed through the Food Bank For NYC network, including nearly 31 million pounds of produce.

Since 2019, visits to New York City food pantries have increased by 82%. Meanwhile the Trump administration has slashed the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) and caused prices for groceries to skyrocket. More than 1.6 million people in New York City rely on SNAP, but with new expanded work requirements and eligibility rules, 223,000 New Yorkers are at risk of losing food assistance. Additionally, with the federal government shifting substantial SNAP costs to states, New York State, counties, and the city will be on the hook for an estimated $1.3 billion in administrative and benefits costs annually.

title: Gillibrand, Colleagues Demand Answers From Hegseth On Cost Of Iran War
text:
Pentagon Greatly Underestimates Cost of Iran War to Taxpayers and Families 

U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), a member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, joined 45 of her colleagues, nearly the entire Democratic caucus, in sending a letter to Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth demanding a full accounting of the costs of the ongoing war with Iran. The letter also criticized the Department of Defense (DoD) for withholding basic budget information from Congress and the American public even as U.S. casualties and taxpayer costs continue to increase. 

“Secretary Hegseth’s tenure at DoD continues to be marred by blatant carelessness and incompetent leadership that has endangered our troops, jeopardized our national security, and left working families paying higher costs,” said Senator Gillibrand. “Now he is asking for tens of billions more to fund President Trump’s reckless war while refusing to reveal its true cost. That is completely unacceptable, and Secretary Hegseth must be held accountable and give taxpayers a straight answer about how this administration is spending their hard-earned money.”

The United States is now more than six months into a conflict President Trump initially said would last six weeks. Eighteen American servicemembers have been killed and more than 820 wounded, and over 50,000 troops are currently deployed to the Middle East. In the letter, Gillibrand and her colleagues note that deployments, including for the USS Lincoln and the 82nd Airborne, have been repeatedly extended, and that their offices have heard directly from military families worried about loved ones serving in the conflict. 

“At home, American taxpayers have already paid an extra $100 billion out of their pockets for higher gas and diesel prices alone and at least another $60 billion in higher costs for things like groceries, mortgages, and plane tickets as a result of the war,” the senators wrote. “Now you are asking that they pay again to fund a war of choice that Congress never authorized and the President launched with no strategic plan.” 

In their letter, the senators highlight the contrast between the current Pentagon’s transparency record with past wartime practice, noting that Hegseth has briefed Congress only seven times in six months and held just eight Pentagon press briefings or interviews since the war began, compared to more than 70 press briefings in the first month of the Iraq War alone. The senators also criticized the administration’s public supplemental funding request as a seven-page document offering only vague line items, in contrast to the detailed, hundred-page supplemental requests provided to Congress during the Iraq and Afghanistan wars. 

Gillibrand and the senators are requesting that the Department of Defense provide: 

A detailed breakdown of all direct and indirect costs of military operations against Iran to date, including damage to installations, aircraft, and equipment. 

A full accounting of the $67 billion supplemental request, specifying what covers past costs versus future operations. 

A detailed plan for how the Pentagon intends to spend the remaining $34 billion from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. 

“Despite asking for tens of billions of additional taxpayer dollars, you have so far failed to provide basic information on how this money has and will be spent,” the senators continued. “Congress must have access to this information to carry out our oversight responsibilities. It is the bare minimum that any American would expect in balancing their own household budget.” 

Senator Gillibrand has repeatedly pressed the administration to disclose the true harm of President Trump’s Iran war. In July, she called out Hegseth over the Pentagon’s inaccurate public casualty reporting, pushing for a full and accurate accounting of the human cost of the war, and demanded the release of DoD’s long-delayed investigation into the U.S. strike on an Iranian elementary school that killed more than 100 children. She also pushed for hearings after reports that service members aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln were left without adequate food and medical care.

In addition to Senator Gillibrand, the letter was signed by Senators Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Michael Bennet (D-CO), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Maria Cantwell (D-WA), Chris Coons (D-DE), Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Richard Durbin (D-IL), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Maggie Hassan (D-NH), Martin Heinrich (D-NM), John Hickenlooper (D-CO), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), Tim Kaine (D-VA), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Andy Kim (D-NJ), Angus King (I-ME), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), Ben Ray Luján (D-NM), Ed Markey (D-MA), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Chris Murphy (D-CT), Patty Murray (D-WA), Jon Ossoff (D-GA), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Gary Peters (D-MI), Jack Reed (D-RI), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), Bernie Sanders (I-VT), Brian Schatz (D-HI), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Elissa Slotkin (D-MI), Tina Smith (D-MN), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Mark Warner (D-VA), Raphael Warnock (D-GA), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Peter Welch (D-VT), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), and Ron Wyden (D-OR).

title: Gillibrand, Bipartisan Group Of Colleagues Demand Trump Administration Release All Documents From U.S.-Saudi Nuclear Deal
text:
U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) joined a bipartisan group of senators to press the Trump administration to declassify and publicly release the two side letters accompanying the proposed U.S.-Saudi civil nuclear cooperation agreement, referred to as a “123 agreement.”

The Trump administration recently submitted the 123 agreement to Congress—as is required by law—but while the agreement references the side letters, the letters themselves are classified, which is unprecedented. Because the side letters affect the obligations and operation of the underlying agreement, Congress and the public cannot fully assess what the United States and Saudi Arabia have agreed to without seeing them.

“Transparency is the only path to truth,” said Senator Gillibrand. “Protecting our national security is of the utmost importance, and a nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia has serious implications for it. There is no justification for hiding key parts of this agreement from the public. As part of our constitutional oversight responsibilities, we are demanding that the Trump administration declassify and release these side letters without delay so the American people get the transparency and accountability they deserve.”

In their letter to U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright, the bipartisan group of senators wrote: “Congress has a statutory responsibility under Section 123 of the Atomic Energy Act to review the proposed nuclear deal, which seeks to facilitate nuclear cooperation with significant implications for U.S. national security interests. Access to the full text is required for the Senate and the public to have a clear understanding of the commitments being made on the nation’s behalf and those being made by Saudi Arabia to the United States.”

“Transparency and open debate are cornerstones of our democracy,” the senators continued. “Congress and the American public must have a meaningful opportunity to review and debate the key components of the U.S.-Saudi nuclear deal before it potentially enters into force. To that end, we call on you to declassify and release the two side letters without delay.”

Senator Gillibrand, a member of the Senate Armed Services and Intelligence Committees, has long fought for transparency and oversight around nuclear weapons policy. She led 26 senators in urging President Trump to preserve key nuclear arms control treaties during his first term, and earlier this year, she introduced legislation that would bring much-needed oversight to the military’s use of AI, including banning its use to launch nuclear weapons. She also demanded that the Trump administration give Congress a full intelligence briefing on its strikes last year against Iran’s nuclear facilities.

In addition to Senator Gillibrand, the letter was signed by U.S. Senators Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Edward Markey (D-MA), Rand Paul (R-KY), John Kennedy (R-LA), Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Jack Reed (D-RI), Patty Murray (D-WA), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), Bernie Sanders (I-VT), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Tim Kaine (D-VA), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Michael Bennet (D-CO), Ron Wyden (D-OR), and Peter Welch (D-VT).

The full text of the letter is available here.

title: ICYMI: Gillibrand Joins Leaders Of NY Food Banks To Call Out Trump Administration’s Massive Cuts To Federal Snap Funding
text:

New York State Will Be Responsible for Estimated $168 Million More Annually as SNAP Cost Responsibilities Shift to State and Local Governments

In case you missed it, on Monday, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand stood with CEOs from food banks around the state to call out the change in Trump’s “Big Beautiful Bill” that will imminently shift billions of dollars in Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) cost responsibilities from the federal government onto state and local governments, resulting in major financial burdens on New York State. This comes as President Trump’s reckless war in Iran and chaotic tariffs have raised grocery prices for New York families and made it increasingly difficult to put food on the table.

“President Trump has consistently threatened and cut the essential services that serve as the backbone of our nation,” said Senator Gillibrand. “At a time when people can barely afford a cart of groceries or a tank of gas, this president is making states and localities bear excruciating cost burdens for SNAP programming while he is funding tax cuts for the richest people in the country and pouring billions into a war overseas.”

The change, which is slated to take effect on October 1 and is part of a broader slate of harmful cuts to the SNAP program, will reduce the federal share of SNAP administrative expenses from 50% to 25%, with states and localities now responsible for covering 75% costs. Counties in New York State are expected to be on the hook for $168 million annually as a result. 

“It’s a cut that we’re really going to struggle to weather,” City Harvest CEO Jilly Stephens told News12.

More than 2.7 million New Yorkers rely on SNAP to feed their families each month. Without this additional federal support, counties across the state may be forced to raise local taxes or slow down the review of SNAP applications.

“You can think about it in terms of funding, but how we want you to think about it is less food on tables, and less food in lunchboxes,” Kristine Borok, president and CEO of Feeding Westchester, told News12.

title: Gillibrand Holds First Ever Congressional Hearing On Menopause
text:
**Watch The Hearing Here**

Today, U.S. Senators Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) and Rick Scott (R-FL), ranking member and chairman of the U.S. Senate Special Committee on Aging, held the first ever congressional hearing on menopause. At the hearing, expert witnesses testified about the urgent need to improve menopause research, training, and care.

Additionally, Gillibrand and Scott made a bipartisan request to the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to investigate how the federal government currently coordinates and funds menopause research and care.

“Menopause impacts over half of our population, and the fact that Congress has never held a hearing on it is absolutely disgraceful,” said Senator Gillibrand. “Today’s hearing was a critical step toward getting this issue front and center so that we can find the best ways to improve research, training, and care for women experiencing menopause. I am committed to working with all of my colleagues—men and women, Democrats and Republicans—to meet the moment on menopause.”

Menopause is one of the most under-researched, undertreated, and underdiagnosed fields of medicine. Women in midlife make up about a third of the U.S. population. However, less than 1% of federal women’s health research funding is allocated to menopause. Additionally, 80% of OB-GYN residents admit to being ill-prepared to discuss menopause—meaning that women who seek medical care for symptoms of menopause are often left untreated.

The lack of treatment for menopause also has massive economic implications. A study by the Mayo Clinic found that menopause costs the U.S. economy $26.6 billion per year, including $1.8 billion in lost work time alone. One in ten women leave the workforce because of menopause, taking decades of knowledge and experience with them.

Gillibrand and Scott’s bipartisan letter to GAO requests a report on the federal government’s role in menopause care and research. This report will help us better understand remaining gaps in menopause-related research, education, and treatment, and what the federal government can do to address these gaps. The text of the letter can be found here.

title: Watch: Gillibrand Demands Immediate Action On Artificial Intelligence, Tariffs, And Menopause Care In CNN Interview
text:
***Watch Senator Gillibrand’s Full Interview Here***

Today, in an interview on CNN’s The Situation Room, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) called for immediate congressional action on regulating artificial intelligence, repealing President Trump’s 50% tariffs on Canada, and providing sufficient healthcare to the millions of American women going through menopause.

The interview follows Senator Gillibrand introducing the BAD DEAL Act to repeal and refund Trump’s 50% Canadian tariffs, and it comes ahead of the first ever congressional hearing on menopause that Gillibrand, ranking member of the Senate Special Committee on Aging, is holding tomorrow.

Footage of Senator Gillibrand’s interview with Pamela Brown can be found here.

Transcripts of key moments can be found below:

ON THE URGENT NEED FOR CONGRESS TO PLACE GUARDRAILS ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE THAT PUT HUMANITY FIRST:

GILLIBRAND: We need urgent engagement now. We need to be able to have rules of the road, we need to be able to have reliable guardrails, and we need to be able to be talking to these AI companies regularly about how to do this well, how to maintain our leadership, how to maintain the ability to cure cancer and cure disease, and have massive breakthroughs. But we also need to make sure we’re investing in America. We need to make sure we are investing the wealth of AI into a jobs guarantee, into healthcare and education. We need to make sure that we have a plan for how we deal with these models that are doing things that even the experts did not expect them able to do so soon. And so we do need that regulatory clarity now, and we need to work with AI companies. And I do not think President Trump is providing any leadership on this. He’s sold the most efficient chips to China, but again, not making sure that we have rules of the road that our own AI companies can ensure that the public is safe. 

BROWN: He’s calling these warnings from these AI leaders a conspiracy. I’m wondering, in your view, does Congress have the sense of urgency that is needed right now to meet this moment, given all the warnings we’re hearing from AI leaders?

GILLIBRAND: I think we should begin hearings immediately. I also think we should work on a bipartisan basis to provide the guidelines and oversight that is needed. AI companies have been, many of them have been asking for this level of engagement and regulation. We’ve seen so many of the harms, but we also have so much promise, and so we want to make sure we’re at the forefront of this technology, that we are competitive, that we can cure cancer and cure other diseases, but we also want to make sure it doesn’t harm humanity, and so that means alignment has to be there. These AI models must be aligned with humanity. Humanity has to be the focus. I worked in our defense bill over the last several months to try to put a human in the loop on all systems and to make sure AI couldn’t be used for domestic surveillance. We wanted to make sure that nuclear weapons would have proper human oversight before an AI model could choose a target or push send on a nuclear weapon. We also wanted to make sure there was humans in the loop for any offensive weapons. Like, I fully understand how efficient and capable an AI system will be for defense to shoot down missiles on their way to American cities, but when you’re talking about choosing a target or deciding when to bomb or where to bomb, that should have a human oversight in all circumstances.

ON GILLIBRAND’S BAD DEAL ACT TO REPEAL AND REFUND PRESIDENT TRUMP’S TARIFFS:

BROWN: You and Senator Peter Welch recently introduced this act to repeal the 50% tariffs placed on Canadian goods and refund Americans for all duties paid. How will this legislation practically manage the logistics of refunding Americans, the taxes they’ve already paid. How would this work?

GILLIBRAND: Well, what the bill is that Senator Welch and I have would repeal these tariffs completely. President Trump has created so much chaos in the market because of these tariffs. In Canada, this new 50% tariff is going to raise prices for New Yorkers on food, on clothing, on everyday household goods, and on building materials, which again will increase the rate of housing and how much it costs to get a better apartment to rent or to buy a home. And so we are trying to repeal those tariffs immediately because what President Trump has done is illegal and creating massive chaos in the economy for everyday New Yorkers and everyday Americans.

ON GILLIBRAND HOLDING THE FIRST EVER CONGRESSIONAL HEARING ON MENOPAUSE:

BROWN: Before we let you go, Senator, I want to ask you about you recently making history by convening the first ever congressional hearing on menopause through the Senate Committee on Aging. Tell us why that was so important to you to bring this issue to light.

GILLIBRAND: Well, menopause is what millions of American women go through. 75 million women are either in perimenopause, menopause, or postmenopause in America today, and the inadequate amount of research and analysis and care for these women is literally disgraceful. It’s basic health care for most Americans, and because it is so underresearched and underresourced, a lot of American women don’t know how to best treat their symptoms. The symptoms can be wide-ranging to debilitating, and women have the right to get access to healthcare to make them be able to function in life, to be able to continue to work, continue to thrive, continue to provide for their families. But because of the lack of research, because of the lack of funding, because of the lack of information and availability of treatments, a lot of women needlessly suffer and are unable to live full lives.

###

title: Sens. Gillibrand And Welch, Rep. Schneider Introduce Bill To Repeal And Refund President Trump’s Canadian Tariffs
text:
**WATCH: Gillibrand Discusses the BAD DEAL Act on CNN**

Today, U.S. Senators Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) and Peter Welch (D-VT) formally introduced the Banning Antiquated Duties and Delivering Equitable American Levies (BAD DEAL) Act to repeal all tariffs levied under Section 338 of the Tariff Act and refund Americans for all duties paid under this authority. This includes President Trump’s 50% tariffs on Canada.

Gillibrand previously announced the bill in August, when Rep. Brad Schneider (D-IL-10) introduced companion legislation in the U.S. House of Representatives. Senators Jacky Rosen (D-NV) and Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) also cosponsor the bill. 

A trade war with Canada will be detrimental to New York’s economy. Canada is one of New York State’s largest export markets for both goods and services, and the state imports more than $20 billion annually from Canada. Already, New York families have spent over $5,500 more due to President Trump’s tariff chaos and other reckless policies. These new 50% tariffs on Canada are projected to cost businesses and households across the U.S. up to $10 billion annually.

“President Trump and Republicans promised to lower costs and make life more affordable, but they’ve used their total power in Washington to make life more expensive than ever,” said Senator Gillibrand. “Let’s be clear: the latest tariffs against Canada are a bad deal for New York families. I’m proud to introduce this legislation to end these costly tariffs and refund Americans. It’s past time for President Trump to stop the political games, get back to the negotiation table, and make a deal that lowers costs and strengthens our economy.”

“No good will come of this trade war with Canada. The only thing these tariffs will create is economic pain on both sides of the border, especially for Vermont and the other 33 states that rely on Canada as their largest trading partner,” said Senator Welch. “Imposing on-again, off-again tariffs is the opposite of how we should treat our close friends and longtime allies, but it’s endemic to how the Trump Administration operates. I’m proud to join my colleagues in leading the BAD DEAL Act to repeal these reckless tariffs and reclaim Congress’ constitutional role in setting our trade policy.”

“Canada is Illinois’ largest trading partner. The costly tariffs imposed under Section 338 by Trump hurt everyone and help no one,” said Rep. Schneider. “American families are actively struggling to make ends meet and have had enough of President Trump’s trade war. I’m proud to join my colleagues to introduce the BAD DEAL Act to repeal this outdated tariff authority and issue the refunds Americans deserve. We must rein in Trump’s chaotic and cost-raising tariffs now before he damages our relationship with our friends and neighbors for years to come.”

The president’s tariffs have previously been found to be unconstitutional and have already raised costs on New Yorkers. Poll after poll after poll have found that a resounding majority of Americans oppose Trump’s tariffs actions that have raised prices and hurt their families.

Senator Gillibrand has opposed President Trump’s tariffs since the start of his administration and worked tirelessly to get the American people their money back. Last year, she joined 14 of her colleagues in introducing the Small Business RELIEF Act to end Trump’s Tariff Tax and refund small businesses their duties paid. In March, she and her colleagues introduced the Small Business Liberation 2.0 Act to exempt small businesses from another set of Trump-imposed tariffs and refund what they had already paid.

The full text of the BAD DEAL Act can be found here.

title: Gillibrand, Garbarino Introduce Bipartisan Legislation To Reimburse Public Retirement Systems For 9/11-Related Disability And Death Benefits
text:
This week, Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) and Congressman Andrew R. Garbarino (R-NY-02) introduced bipartisan, bicameral legislation to reimburse public employee retirement systems for costs associated with accidental disability retirements and accidental deaths resulting from the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center. Garbarino and Gillibrand were joined by Senator Chuck Schumer (D-NY) and Representatives Nicole Malliotakis (R-NY-11), Jerry Nadler (D-NY-12), and Dan Goldman (D-NY-10) as co-leads. 

Twenty-five years after September 11th, thousands of first responders and others who participated in rescue and cleanup operations continue to suffer from illnesses and injuries connected to their service at Ground Zero. As more members of the 9/11 community have developed serious health conditions or lost their lives to 9/11-related illnesses, public employee retirement systems have faced growing costs associated with disability retirement and death benefits.

The legislation would authorize $5.9134 billion for the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to reimburse eligible public employee retirement systems for those costs. To qualify, a retirement system must include a member who participated in rescue, recovery, or cleanup operations resulting from the September 11 attacks on the World Trade Center. Reimbursements would be restricted for use by the eligible retirement systems.

“Twenty-five years after the darkest day in our nation’s history, we must continue to honor our promise to never forget,” said Senator Gillibrand. “The victims of September 11th are not just the men and women killed on that terrible day – countless American lives continue to be claimed by illnesses linked to the attacks. With New York pension systems facing a shortfall as a result, we must act now to ensure those injured and sickened from recovery efforts and the families of our heroes are not worried about receiving every dollar they deserve. I am grateful this bill has strong bipartisan support in both the House and Senate, and I will work with my colleagues to get it swiftly passed and signed into law.”

“Twenty-five years after September 11th, New York is still carrying costs from that terrible day, just as responders and their families are still living with its consequences,” said Congressman Garbarino. “The men and women who ran toward danger and spent months working at Ground Zero did so without hesitation. As more of them have become sick or lost their lives because of that work, New York’s public retirement systems have rightfully provided the disability and death benefits they earned. The federal government has a responsibility to help cover the costs directly tied to the attacks. Senator Gillibrand and I are committed to making sure New York and the 9/11 community are not left to shoulder that burden alone.”

“‘Never forget’ is not just a slogan. It’s a promise to stand by our 9/11 heroes and their families for as long as it takes, and that promise includes making sure the pensions they and their families are owed are never shortchanged. Just days after our city marked the 25th anniversary of 9/11, I’m proud to support this bill so the federal government continues to do its part and support our first responders who rushed to help at our city’s darkest hour,” said Senator Schumer. 

“New York’s pension systems have proudly stood behind the survivors and first responders of the September 11th attacks, especially as they developed illnesses because of their service that day. But that support has come at a steep cost, and it’s time for the federal government to help carry the load. I’m proud to co-lead this legislation, which would reimburse New York’s pension systems for the costs of supporting our 9/11 heroes. These brave Americans deserve our eternal gratitude, and this bill helps make good on that promise,” said Congressman Dan Goldman. 

“Twenty-five years after September 11th, we must continue standing with the first responders and members of the 9/11 community who risked their lives during the rescue, recovery, and cleanup efforts. I’m proud to join my colleagues in supporting this bipartisan legislation to honor their heroism and sacrifice and ensure they and their families receive the benefits they earned and deserve. We will never forget,” said Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis. 

“On September 11, 2001, New York City’s bravest and finest ran toward the danger to rescue neighbors and strangers alike. In the days, weeks, and months that followed, thousands more helped clean and rebuild Lower Manhattan. It is our duty to honor the sacrifices of the first responders of 9/11 by making sure these heroes and their families can receive the pensions they earned,” said Congressman Jerry Nadler.

“Fully funding the World Trade Center Health Program has been a priority for the union movement, but more work remains. This bipartisan legislation addresses the continued costs of the September 11th terrorist attacks on the New York State and City Pension systems. The federal government must reimburse the State and City for costs related to death and disability payments. Failing to cover these costs unfairly threatens future retirees’ pensions. We are deeply grateful for the leadership of Rep. Garbarino, Senator Gillibrand, and the entire New York delegation in ensuring the federal government follows through on its responsibility to cover all costs related to the attacks,” said Mario Cilento, President of the New York State AFL-CIO. 

“The recent disclosures from the City of New York show that we are still learning about the full extent of the health effects of the toxic chemicals at Ground Zero. Congressman Garbarino (R-NY) and Senators Gillibrand (D-NY), Schumer (D-NY), and their colleagues deserve our thanks for working to introduce bipartisan legislation dealing with the increased costs to the New York pension systems of those who are retiring and some who are dying because of the health effects of 9/11—just part of the continuing costs of that day, both in lives and health impacts, 25 years later,” said Ben Chavet, Executive Director of the Citizens for Extension of the James Zadroga Act. 

“25 years after the 9/11 Terror Attacks, New York City still primarily shoulders the responsibility of caring for our fallen brothers and sisters and those forced into early retirement. I thank Senator Gillibrand and Representative Garbarino for fighting to secure the federal funding needed to strengthen the pensions of those who stood on the front lines of public safety that day. This critical legislation will ensure that the costs of 9/11-related deaths and medical retirements will no longer be borne by New York City and State alone. I urge Congress to pass this important legislation as soon as possible,” said IAFF General President Edward Kelly.

“The terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001, were an attack upon our nation, and the heroism displayed by New York’s first responders during the rescue and recovery efforts that followed gave all Americans the hope and the strength to rebuild,” said President Vincent Vallelong of the NYPD Sergeants Benevolent Association. “On numerous occasions, Congress has recognized the federal government’s obligation to support these brave men and women through programs such as the World Trade Center Health Program and Victim Compensation Fund. Like those efforts, this legislation recognizes that the extraordinary pension costs resulting from a national terrorist attack are a federal responsibility and will ensure that NYPD officers, retirees, and their families receive the benefits they have earned. We are grateful for the leadership of Rep. Garbarino, Sen. Gillibrand, and their colleagues for introducing this bill, and we urge Congress to swiftly enact it into law.”

The bill requires the FEMA Administrator to reimburse eligible public employee retirement systems for costs related to accidental disability retirements and accidental deaths resulting from participation in the rescue, recovery, or cleanup operations following the September 11 attacks. It authorizes $5,913,400,000 for Fiscal Year 2027 to carry out the reimbursements.

Garbarino and Gillibrand have consistently worked together on a bipartisan basis to support the 9/11 community and ensure responders and their families receive the benefits and care they have earned.

title: In Westchester: Gillibrand, Leaders of Food Banks Statewide Raise Alarm On Trump Administration Slashing Federal Funding For SNAP And Threatening New Yorkers’ Benefits
text:
New York State Will Be Responsible for Estimated $168 Million More Annually as SNAP Cost Responsibilities Shift to State and Local Governments

Today, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand joined CEOs from food banks around the state to gaggle with reporters regarding the change in Trump’s “Big Beautiful Bill” that will imminently shift billions of dollars in Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) cost responsibilities from the federal government onto state and local governments, resulting in major financial burdens on New York State. This comes as President Trump’s reckless war in Iran and chaotic tariffs have raised grocery prices for New York families and made it increasingly difficult to put food on the table.

“President Trump has consistently threatened and cut the essential services that serve as the backbone of our nation,” said Senator Gillibrand. “At a time when people can barely afford a cart of groceries or a tank of gas, this president is making states and localities bear excruciating cost burdens for SNAP programming while he is funding tax cuts for the richest people in the country and pouring billions into a war overseas.”

“The recent decrease in SNAP enrollment does not mean hunger is disappearing in Westchester County, across New York State, or anywhere in our country; it means fewer people are getting the food they need,” said Kristine Borok, President and CEO of Feeding Westchester. “Right now, 41% of Westchester households are at risk of hunger, and that number is growing. The inability of families working full-time jobs to put food on the table is not a fleeting occurrence; it has become a change in our society. The food banks represented here today, and our network of partners across Westchester County and New York State, are committed to doing everything in our power to make sure no one in our community goes hungry. To be clear: food banks would need to double or triple our distribution to replace the SNAP cuts. Our network was never meant to replace the federal safety net. Food banks were built as an emergency response system, not a permanent substitute for federal nutrition programs, and we cannot absorb cuts of this magnitude on top of the rising cost of living.”

The change, which is slated to take effect on October 1 and is part of a broader slate of harmful cuts to the SNAP program, will reduce the federal share of SNAP administrative expenses from 50% to 25%, with states and localities now responsible for covering 75% costs. Counties in New York State are expected to be on the hook for $168 million annually as a result, with Westchester County being responsible for an additional $4.5 million to keep SNAP-supported programs running. More than 65,000 people in Westchester County rely on SNAP to feed their families each month. Without this additional federal support, counties may be forced to raise local taxes or slow down the review of SNAP applications.

title: In Schenectady, Gillibrand Rails Against Closure of Veterans Affairs Community Based Outpatient Clinic
text:
1,500 Capital Region Veterans’ Care Disrupted

Despite Repeated Requests for Answers, the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs Has Provided Little Transparency and Communication on the Future of Capital Region Veterans’ Services

Today, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, held a press conference addressing the recent closure of the Schenectady Veterans Affairs (VA) Community Based Outpatient Clinic (CBOC). This is the region’s second CBOC closure in five years, following the shutdown of the Troy CBOC in July 2021, forcing veterans to seek alternative healthcare in places that may be far from their homes.

“The Schenectady VA provided access to care for more than 1,500 veterans in the Capital Region who put their lives on the line to protect our nation,” said Senator Gillibrand. “The decision to close this facility with little communication on alternative care could have devastating consequences. Veterans served our country, and we have a duty and responsibility to ensure their care. I have repeatedly demanded answers from VA Secretary Doug Collins, and I want to reiterate that any plans going forward must include the veterans who have relied on the care of the Schenectady VA.”

“The federal VA closed our Schenectady Clinic despite months of warnings from veterans and repeated calls to stop this decision,” said Assemblyman Angelo Santabarbara. “The VA’s own records show that cost and projected savings were part of the plan. The bottom line is our veterans should never be asked to pay the price for federal cost-cutting. The lack of answers and communication throughout this process was unacceptable. Veterans deserved answers, not excuses, and access to care, not another barrier standing in their way. At the very least, the VA should have paused the closure, met with us and listened to the veterans who depended on this clinic. The doors may be closed, but the fight is not over. I will continue standing with our veterans and fighting to restore the local access to health care that this closure stripped away.”

“As Rotterdam Town Supervisor, I stand firmly against the closing of the Schenectady VA Clinic,” said Rotterdam Town Supervisor John Polimeni. “This decision, overseen by VA Secretary Doug Collins, abandons the men and women who wore our nation’s uniform and now face greater barriers to the care they were promised. I have repeatedly requested meetings with VA staff and have offered practical solutions to keep services accessible locally, yet those concerns have gone unanswered. Our veterans deserve better than to be pushed farther from care and treated as a budget line instead of as heroes who have earned our unwavering support.” 

The closure of the Schenectady VA Clinic is a slap in the face to those who sacrifice everything for this country and runs contradictory to our shared commitment to caring for all of our veterans when they return home,” said State Senator Patricia Fahy. “Schenectady County veterans should not have to travel further or pay more to access the basic services afforded to them after their service is complete. Our community has not been and will not be silent while this federal administration rips away healthcare from veterans at a time when access to quality, affordable healthcare is dwindling. Our message is clear: reverse this decision and continue your commitment to serving our Schenectady County veterans and meet them where they are in our community.” 

“The closure of the Schenectady VA clinic is a serious concern for Veterans across the Capital Region who relied on that facility for their care,” said Albany County Executive Daniel P. McCoy. “Our Veterans should not face additional barriers or uncertainty when it comes to accessing the health care they earned through their service. I share Senator Gillibrand’s concerns and believe the VA must provide clear answers and a plan that ensures continuity of care for every Veteran affected by this closure.”

“The VA clinic in Rotterdam provided care to more than 1,500 veterans. Now, those veterans are dealing with the impact of its closure, including challenges finding transportation to get to another clinic and uncertainty about who will provide their care going forward,” said Schenectady County Legislature Chairman Gary Hughes. “Our veterans served and sacrificed for our country. They earned these benefits, and we have a responsibility to make sure they can access the care they need. We thank Senator Gillibrand for standing up for our veterans and bringing us together to make sure their voices are heard.”

When the closure was announced in March 2026, Gillibrand immediately called on the Secretary of Veterans Affairs Doug Collins to halt the closure and provide immediate answers to ensure that healthcare would not be disrupted for the over 1,500 Capital Region veterans who relied on this clinic. Now, six months following the original letter, and after a subsequent follow-up letter in August, few questions have been answered, even as the VA has closed the clinic.

###

The post In Schenectady, Gillibrand Rails Against Closure of Veterans Affairs Community Based Outpatient Clinic appeared first on Kirsten Gillibrand | U.S. Senator for New York.

title: Amid New York Fashion Week, Gillibrand, Nadler Reintroduce FABRIC Act To Bring Accountability And Transparency To The Fashion Industry
text:
Today, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) and Congressman Jerry Nadler (D-NY-12) announced the reintroduction of their Fashioning Accountability and Building Real Institutional Change (FABRIC) Act. In New York State, there are approximately 130,000 people employed by the fashion industry, including thousands working in apparel manufacturing. Garment workers are a cornerstone of the American economy, and for far too long, they have faced unsafe working conditions, wage theft, and piecework pay, which often prioritizes fast fashion over the safety of workers. Gillibrand and Nadler’s FABRIC Act would protect over 75,000 American garment workers and help revitalize the garment manufacturing industry in the United States by improving working conditions and reforming the piece-rate pay scale. 

“Garment workers are the backbone of a multibillion-dollar industry, yet for far too long, their labor has been undervalued and exploited,” said Senator Gillibrand. “We cannot champion American innovation while turning a blind eye to abusive labor practices in our own backyard. It’s time to take bold action at the federal level to change the fabric of the American garment industry. The United States was once home to a booming apparel manufacturing industry, and it’s time to reexamine how this industry has evolved over the past 50 years and change how we treat our workers. With the FABRIC Act, we can curb wage theft, protect our workers, and revitalize domestic manufacturing so that ‘Made in America’ also means ethically made.”

“America’s garment workers have been undervalued and subjected to unfair labor practices for far too long, due to weak regulations across the fashion industry and the rise of fast fashion. With more than 100,000 New Yorkers contributing their labor to a billion-dollar garment industry, it is time to protect these workers and others across our nation and make historic investments in domestic manufacturing by passing the FABRIC Act,” said Congressman Jerrold Nadler. “I’m proud to work with Senator Gillibrand to protect workers’ rights, bring jobs back from overseas, and revitalize the American fashion industry.”

The FABRIC Act proposes to address these issues by:

Restructuring pay rates for garment workers and providing minimum wage as a floor with productivity incentives on top.

Establishing new liability measures that compel major retailers to become allies in combating workplace violations.

Introducing recordkeeping and transparency measures, including requiring garment manufacturers and contractors operating in the U.S. to register with the Department of Labor.

Incentivizing reshoring by creating a domestic garment manufacturing grant program aimed at revitalizing the industry.

title: Gillibrand Announces Bipartisan Resolution Commemorating 25th Anniversary of September 11, 2001 Terror Attacks
text:
Today, on the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand led a bipartisan group of her colleagues in announcing a Senate resolution honoring the victims, first responders, and survivors of 9/11, as well as the service members who defended the United States in the aftermath. The resolution pays tribute to the 2,977 individuals killed in Lower Manhattan, at the Pentagon, and in Shanksville, Pennsylvania. It also honors the 343 firefighters, 72 law enforcement officers, 8 emergency medical technicians and paramedics, and 55 military personnel at the Pentagon who sacrificed their lives responding to the attacks, alongside the passengers and crew of United Airlines Flight 93. The resolution also recognizes the charitable foundations, nonprofit organizations, labor organizations, faith-based organizations, and community groups that have faithfully served survivors and families of victims. 

“Twenty-five years ago, our nation experienced tragedy, but in our darkest hour, we saw the extraordinary courage and resilience of the American people,” said Senator Gillibrand.“As we mark 25 years since September 11, 2001, we owe it to the victims, the heroes who ran into the burning towers, and the military personnel who answered the call to serve to ensure their sacrifices are never forgotten. This resolution reaffirms our commitment to standing with survivors and their families, supporting the programs that continue to provide critical care, and vowing to never forget.” 

Throughout her time in Congress, Senator Gillibrand has continuously advocated for 9/11first responders and survivors, championing major federal efforts to secure permanent healthcare and financial compensation. She led the passage of the James Zadroga 9/11Health and Compensation Act of 2010 to establish the World Trade Center Health Program (WTCHP) and reopen the Victim Compensation Fund (VCF). She also spearheaded the passage of long-term protections for the 9/11 community with the James Zadroga 9/11Health and Compensation Reauthorization Act to extend the WTCHP through 2090, co-authored the Never Forget the Heroes Act of 2019 to permanently fund the VCF, and led legislative fixes to stabilize the WTCHP’s budget formula, ensuring that over 140,000 enrolled responders and survivors maintain access to specialized care and benefits.

In addition to Senator Gillibrand, the resolution is cosponsored by Senators Andy Kim (D-NJ), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Chris Murphy (D-CT), Tim Kaine (D-VA), John Fetterman (D-PA), Mark Warner (D-VA), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Chuck Grassley (R-IA), and John Boozman (R-AR).

title: Gillibrand, Colleagues Condemn DOJ’s Failure To Vigorously Defend Fundamental Gun Violence Prevention Law
text:
U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) joined 12 Senate colleagues in condemning the Department of Justice (DOJ)’s refusal to seek immediate appellate relief from a recent district court decision striking down key regulatory requirements of the National Firearms Act of 1934 (NFA).

In a letter to Attorney General Todd Blanche, the senators expressed serious concerns about DOJ’s failure to vigorously defend the NFA, a foundational federal gun violence prevention law that regulates some of the most dangerous concealable weapons in the country.

“As gun violence continues to threaten the safety of our kids, our families, and our police officers, the Trump administration should be doing more to keep guns out of the wrong hands – not less,” said Senator Gillibrand. “Refusing to defend these nearly 100-year-old protections is a direct surrender to the gun lobby at the expense of American lives. It’s absolutely unconscionable, and I am doing everything I can to fight back.”

Last month, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas held unconstitutional the NFA’s regulatory requirements for certain highly dangerous weapons. Although the court temporarily stayed its order to give DOJ time to seek immediate appellate relief, DOJ declined to do so, opting instead to let the court’s injunction take effect.

“DOJ’s failure to seek immediate relief is profoundly concerning—for the integrity of the Department, the rule of law, and the public’s safety,” the senators wrote. “The Department has long recognized its ‘duty to defend the constitutionality of an Act of Congress whenever a reasonable argument can be made in its support.’ During your confirmation proceedings, you reiterated this precise principle—including in the specific context of the NFA.” The senators went on to note that DOJ’s sudden retreat appeared to be the result of a substantial pressure campaign by gun rights lobbyists and a group of Republican lawmakers.

The senators demanded answers about DOJ’s justification for not seeking immediate relief and called on DOJ to appeal the district court’s decision.

“As a result of DOJ’s refusal to seek a stay of the District Court’s order, some of the most dangerous concealable weapons in the country—including those that have been used in several mass shootings—can now be (and have been) bought and sold outside the NFA’s heightened regulatory framework for the first time in nearly 100 years,” the senators concluded. “We urge the Department to resume its vigorous defense of the NFA and fulfill the promises you made to defend the constitutionality of laws passed by Congress and keep Americans safe.”

Senator Gillibrand continues to be a fierce advocate for commonsense gun regulation. She previously wrote the interstate gun trafficking ban that became law as part of the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act, which has led to over 6,000 guns being taken off the streets. When the Trump administration stopped providing updates on the number of alleged traffickers charged under the interstate gun trafficking ban, Gillibrand successfully demanded that DOJ restore transparency and resume the updates. In July, she also called out the Trump administration’s dangerous rollbacks of gun safety regulations like those that block illegal firearm sales and keep guns away from people with a history of mental illness.

In addition to Senator Gillibrand, the letter was signed by Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL) and Senators Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Tim Kaine (D-VA), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Jack Reed (D-RI), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), and Peter Welch (D-VT).

The full text of the letter is available here.

title: Gillibrand Statement On Release Of City Records On Post-9/11 Air Quality In Lower Manhattan
text:
Gillibrand: “There Must Be Accountability. These Records Must Be Released In Full. The 9/11 Community And New York Deserve The Truth About What Was Known And When”

Today, in response to new reports underscoring that New Yorkers were misled about dangerous air quality after the terror attack in New York City on September 11, 2001, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand issued the following statement: 

“In the aftermath of 9/11, our first responders and survivors were told the same thing over and over: prove it. Prove that the dust and smoke you breathed for months at Ground Zero made you sick. Prove that your cancer, your lung disease, your colleague’s death was connected to the cleanup. Dying heroes had to travel to Washington to plead with members of Congress to look them in the eye, believe them, and help them. 

“I have spent my Senate career fighting for these families: passing the Zadroga Act to establish the World Trade Center Health Program, permanently funding the Victim Compensation Fund, and fixing the health program’s funding shortfall. Together, we had to fight to prove what we already knew, and what it appears some officials knew from the very beginning.

“I want to thank Mayor Mamdani and his administration for releasing these initial public records regarding the toxins present during and after the attacks, and for their commitment to fully review and publicize more records over the next year.

“These documents suggest officials had evidence of dangerous conditions – benzene and asbestos spiking in November 2001, and carcinogens present the following summer – while assuring the public there was little long-term risk. Firefighters worked that site for months breathing air the city claimed was safe, but apparently knew was harmful. 

“There must be accountability. These records must be released in full. The 9/11 community and New York deserve the truth about what was known and when. 

“We already know the cost: last week, the FDNY released a report that over 9,000 people – including 600 firefighters – have died from illnesses tied to Ground Zero. Overall, more than 12,000 FDNY members have at least one World Trade Center-related condition, and nearly a quarter of those have been diagnosed with cancer.

“This is also why our fight for the World Trade Center Health Program is not finished. Securing funding was essential, but I will keep pressing the program to fix delays in certifying new conditions, clinical staffing shortages, and administrative backlogs. Nobody who breathed that air should be denied care or have to wait years for it.

“Twenty-five years after one of the darkest days in our nation’s history, we cannot forget the sacrifices and heroism of our first responders and ordinary New Yorkers who ran through flame, rubble, and toxic soot to save lives. Who cleaned up the aftermath and then fought to rebuild New York City stronger than ever. In our nation’s darkest hour, they put on the armor of light. We must never forget their courage, nor can we ignore the toll that that courage took on their health and their families.” 

The World Trade Center Health Program (WTCHP) was established in 2011 as part of the James Zadroga 9/11 Health and Compensation Act and was originally funded for five years at $1.6 billion. The program was reauthorized in 2015 and extended through 2090 with bipartisan support. In 2022, Senator Gillibrand led lawmakers in passing $1 billion for the WTCHP in the end-of-year spending bill, and in 2023, Senator Gillibrand helped secure an additional $676 million for the program. Earlier this year, she successfully secured full funding for the program, continuing her commitment to ensuring 9/11 responders and survivors receive the care they need, now and in the years ahead.

title: Gillibrand Announces Bill To Make Large-Scale Wage Theft A Felony Nationwide
text:
Ahead of Labor Day, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) announced the Don’t Stand for Taking Employed Americans’ Livings (Don’t STEAL) Act, which would make large-scale wage theft a felony nationwide. Representative Seth Magaziner (D-RI-02) and 28 cosponsors have introduced companion legislation in the U.S. House of Representatives.

“Working Americans deserve to take home every penny that they have earned, and employers who cheat their employees out of hard-earned wages must be held accountable,” said Senator Gillibrand. “Ahead of Labor Day, I am proud to announce this bill to bring the punishment for wage theft in line with other forms of criminal theft. This is commonsense legislation to help protect workers, and I am determined to get it passed.”

“It is outrageous that in the United States of America, someone can face jail time for stealing a television but get only a slap on the wrist for stealing wages from a worker’s paycheck,” said Representative Magaziner. “I am grateful to Senator Gillibrand for leading the fight in the Senate to make wage theft a federal crime and hold accountable bad actors who cheat working people out of their hard-earned pay. I look forward to working with her to pass the Don’t STEAL Act in both chambers and get it signed into law.”

Wage theft takes many forms, including employers refusing to pay promised wages, paying subminimum wages, failing to pay for all hours worked, or not paying overtime premiums. Every year, over $15 billion is stolen from workers by their employers. In 2025, the U.S. Department of Labor recovered more than $259 million in back wages and damages owed to 176,957 workers, representing just a fraction of wage theft that occurred that year. This kind of wage theft impacts workers across industries and of all income levels, but it has a more profound impact on low-wage workers, who can least afford to bear the cost of lost earnings.

The Don’t STEAL Act would help protect workers by strengthening penalties for wage theft, bringing them in line with other forms of criminal theft under federal law. Under this legislation, employers who willfully fail to pay wages, deny overtime, or steal tips will face misdemeanor or felony charges depending on the severity of the violation. Currently, wage theft is treated at most as a misdemeanor.

The Don’t STEAL Act also brings penalties for wage theft in line with other common forms of theft under federal law. Today, employers who commit willful wage theft can be fined no more than $10,000. This bill eliminates that cap and requires fines to be proportional to the amount of wages stolen.

This legislation is endorsed by 15 organizations, including AFL-CIO and several other labor unions. Senator Gillibrand plans to formally introduce the Don’t STEAL Act when the Senate returns to session later this month.
